Senses.Explanation: The host within the guest names a guest–host position whose interpretation is explicitly system-dependent in later Chan analysis. In the later systematic account of Linji's four guest-host configurations, this is the configuration named when ‘the student has a nose-hole’ (學人有鼻孔). Records then raise the label as a public question and preserve different answers, including 'facing him, there is no companion.' This is one member of the fourfold set alongside host-within-host, guest-within-host, and guest-within-guest. The texts explicitly say that Linji's guest-host system differs from Caodong's, so the shared graphs must not blur the two school-specific things.

Senses.Note: Separate school-specific referent, not a competing reading of one saying. Variant answers are retained as deployments within the Caodong positional category and are not split further.

Senses.Explanation: This separate sense denotes Caodong host-within-guest position, not Linji host-within-guest configuration. In Caodong guest-host discourse the same words name a position paired with host-within-guest's converse and with the bent-and-upright vocabulary. The Eye of Humans and Gods explicitly glosses Caodong's host-within-guest as 'function within essence' (用中體) and says this fourfold guest-host system is not the same as Linji's. In the Dongshan encounter, Dongshan asks 'what is host within guest?' and receives 'white clouds cover the green mountain'; another transmitted version assigns 'long years not leaving the house.' Later verse can say 'host within guest is precisely guest within host' and tell the hearer not to recognize a fixed pattern in reversal and accord. These are recorded formulas and answers, not an invitation to supply an interpretation beyond them.
